title: test(dogfood): pin the undeclared-key refusal on the suite's SQL driver arms (#15953 slice 7)
body:
Part of #15953
Clause-②: no

## What this is

Slice 7 of the card: row 10 of the classification table (comment `6115219467`), the per-driver half, as the slice-7 claim (`6217542057`) scopes it. It is one new test file, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/undeclared-key-conformance.test.ts`, beside `read-coercion-conformance.test.ts` and in its style.

On every SQL driver arm the dogfood conformance files run, it pins that a key the object does not declare is refused by the ENGINE as one envelope, whether the caller wrote it or a before-hook stamped it. The table, read straight past the engine through knex, holds nothing the refused write carried. This is the platform's own pin for what hotcrm's `test/undeclared-key-probe.test.ts` asserted, so objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1583 can retire that file.

- No source change anywhere.
- `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`, so there is no changeset. The seat applies `skip-changeset`.
- The card stays open for the date-window family's residue and the acceptance clause "runs from `os verify` on hotcrm's metadata".

## The arms

- **`driver-sql` on better-sqlite3 `:memory:`.** This arm is the table's "memory", read as the claim rules: the driver-memory arm left the conformance files in #5704, and this is the arm `read-coercion-conformance.test.ts` runs. It is also the table's "sqlite".
- **`driver-sqlite-wasm` `:memory:`.** Covered by measurement. The suite already runs this arm (`date-bucket-parity-conformance.test.ts`, `group-key-read-shape-parity.test.ts`), and here it boots under `ObjectQL` and syncs its schema.

## What each arm answers today, measured before anything was pinned

The setup is `ObjectQL` over each real driver with a system context. `probe_quote` declares `tax_rate` and `probe_quote_line` does not (hotcrm's declared/undeclared pair). The reading was taken on the built engine and drivers at base `161aee104`, and the pinned file re-ran green at the final head.

| write carrying `tax_rate` onto `probe_quote_line` | driver-sql | sqlite-wasm |
|:--|:--|:--|
| caller insert, caller update | refused: `Error`, `code` `INVALID_FIELD`, `status` 400, `field` `tax_rate`, `object` `probe_quote_line` | the same |
| `beforeInsert` hook stamps it | the same envelope | the same |
| `beforeUpdate` hook, by id | the same envelope | the same |
| `beforeUpdate` hook, by predicate (`multi: true`) | the same envelope | the same |
| the table after each refusal | unchanged | unchanged |
| the same hook on `probe_quote`, which declares the key | stored `7` | stored `7` |

No arm departs from one envelope, so there was no defect to stop at. The objectql pins (`engine-post-hook-undeclared-field.test.ts`, `engine-undeclared-key-caller-path.test.ts`) prove the door against driver doubles only, and say so. This file is the half on the shipped drivers.

## The cases (six per arm, twelve in all)

1. **Control:** a declared key round-trips through insert, update, `findOne` and the knex read.
2. **Control:** the same hook stores the same key on the object that declares it. So a refusal can never mean "hooks never ran on this arm".
3. **Caller insert:** `INVALID_FIELD` / 400, naming the field and the object. The table is empty.
4. **Caller update:** the same envelope, and the row is unchanged.
5. **Hook insert:** `code` and `status` as above, and the same envelope, field for field, as the caller path's answer on that arm. The table is empty.
6. **Hook update, by id and by predicate:** the same, and both rows are unchanged.

The envelope is projected from the engine's own error (`code`, `status`, `field`, `object`) and never rebuilt in the test. The hook path is compared with the caller path's measured answer. No message text is pinned.

## Ablation (one, on the fixture)

- **Mutation:** the probe hook on `probe_quote_line` writes a DECLARED key instead. `const LINE_HOOK_WRITES = { [KEY]: 7 };` becomes `{ unit_price: 7 }`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor x1 to x0, replacement x0 to x1, blob `878a1b97a7cc` to `8c606255f1ce`. A trap in the ablation script restores on exit.
- **Reading:** predicted `4 failed | 8 passed`, read `4 failed | 8 passed`. Both hook-path cases failed on both arms, each with "expected the engine to refuse, and it answered". The controls and the caller path stayed green.
- **Restore:** the blob is back to `878a1b97a7cc`, equal to HEAD's; `git diff HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` are both empty.
- **No build leg:** the mutated file is the test itself, which vitest loads from source, so there was no build or dist leg to run.

## Tests and gates, at `04185a291`

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=verbose test/undeclared-key-conformance.test.ts test/read-coercion-conformance.test.ts`: 2 files, 14 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood typecheck`: exit 0, after a build of the whole `@objectstack/dogfood^...` closure. `tsc --listFiles` includes the new file.
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config packages/qa/dogfood/test/undeclared-key-conformance.test.ts`: exit 0 with 0 messages, and the file was linted, not ignored. The repo-wide lint is CI's `Lint & Repo Gates`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths): 53 derived, 53 run, all exit 0. `--ran` reconciles 53 / 53 / 0 NOT-MEASURED / 0 UNRUN.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: 8 packages outside the dogfood closure had no `dist/`). It exited 0 after those were built.
- **Declared to CI, not run locally:** the rest of the dogfood suite (the Dogfood Regression Gate, three shards) and `test:repo` (Test Core).

## Acceptance notes

- **Wall time.** The twelve cases take about 200 ms. The file's local wall (15 s on a shared box) is module import of the built objectql and drivers. Dogfood is excluded from Test Core, whose per-file captures feed the 10 s line, so this file is outside that reading.
- **A driver-memory arm was not added.** `bootStack({ databaseDriver: 'memory' })` can still boot driver-memory in this suite; the analytics isolation pins use it as a two-driver equivalence arm. This slice follows the claim's reading of "memory". Noted, not filed; carrier: none.
- **`origin/main` moved after the merge.** This branch merged `6d1660dc3`, and `origin/main` then moved to `68ffa5dc1`. That is one commit (PR #23959), touching other dogfood files (`authz-conformance.test.ts` and its census) and `packages/rest`. Neither reads this file or anything it imports, so the branch was not re-merged.
- **Left alone, as the claim says:**
  - the objectql write-path half of row 10 (it landed with #23603);
  - the date-window family's residue;
  - `packages/verify`.
